content_voiceover: This is the NCCN treatment algorithm for peripheral T cell lymphomas, and the key branch point is ALK positive ALCL versus everything else. For ALK positive ALCL, stage one or two disease gets multiagent chemotherapy for six cycles, either alone or combined with involved-site radiotherapy, while stage three or four gets six cycles of multiagent chemotherapy alone. All the other histologies, ALK negative ALCL, PTCL not otherwise specified, enteropathy associated T cell lymphoma, monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T cell lymphoma, angioimmunoblastic T cell lymphoma or nodal TFH lymphoma, and follicular T cell lymphoma, are lumped together and treated similarly regardless of stage, with a strong preference for clinical trial enrollment, or multiagent chemotherapy with or without involved-site radiotherapy. Response is assessed with interim PET/CT after three to four cycles. After completing planned treatment, patients are restaged again with PET/CT. Those in complete response can go to clinical trial, consolidative autologous stem cell transplant, or observation, while partial responders or those with progressive disease escalate therapy. Note the special call-out: autologous HCT should be considered for high IPI ALK positive ALCL even though that subtype otherwise has a favorable prognosis. Long-term follow-up includes surveillance imaging and clinical exams for five years.
keypoints: ALK+ ALCL: staged therapy (I-II vs III-IV); other PTCL histologies treated similarly across stages
Interim restaging with FDG-PET/CT after 3-4 cycles guides ongoing therapy
CR after treatment: consider clinical trial, autologous HCT, or observation
Consider autologous HCT even for high-IPI ALK+ ALCL despite its generally good prognosis
PR or progressive disease triggers relapsed/refractory pathway
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, know the big branch: ALK positive ALCL is staged and generally has the best outcomes, while ALK negative ALCL and the other PTCL histologies are treated more uniformly and considered for clinical trials. Interim and end of treatment PET/CT drive decisions, and consolidative autologous transplant is considered even in high IPI ALK positive disease.
